subject: Clarify whether Oct 1-2 are included in the SOC 2 Type II coverage window
messages:
From: security@acme.com
To: ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-18T08:12:00-04:00
Subject: Question on SOC 2 Type II report dates — inclusivity of Oct 1-2

Hi Ben,

Quick question as we prepare our evidence bundle for procurement: your SOC 2 Type II report lists the monitoring period as Aug 1, 2025 through Sep 30, 2026 (report dated Sep 30, 2026). Our team in EMEA recorded an incident on Oct 1 00:15 UTC and another related event on Oct 2 23:50 UTC. Before we start pulling logs, can you confirm whether Redwood interprets the report coverage as inclusive of full calendar months (i.e., up to and including Sep 30 23:59:59 in UTC), or whether there was any point-in-time snapshot or sampling that might have captured data on Oct 1-2?

Specifically: 
- Were there any control changes after Sep 30 that would exclude early-October telemetry from the certified period?
- If Oct 1-2 are outside the certified window, do you provide a bridge letter or post-period confirmation covering Oct 1-15?

We may need logs covering Oct 1-2 if you can include them via a short bridge confirmation. Appreciate a fast turnaround — procurement is on a tight timeline.

Cheers,
Dawn Park
Senior InfoSec Manager, Acme Corp
attachments: none
From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: security@acme.com
Cc: dawn@acme.com
Date: 2026-10-18T10:05:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Question on SOC 2 Type II report dates — inclusivity of Oct 1-2

Hi Dawn — thanks for the clear question. Short answer: Oct 1-2 are outside the formal SOC 2 Type II period we certified (which ends at 23:59:59 UTC on 2026-09-30). Our auditor used month-end inclusivity for the reporting period, and the independent report covers Aug 1, 2025 — Sep 30, 2026.

Longer context and options: 
- The certified period is inclusive through the end of Sep 30, 2026 UTC. After that point we are outside the attested timeframe.
- Redwood can provide a bridge letter (conditional) that confirms there were no material changes to the control environment through a limited post-period window (we typically offer Oct 1—Oct 15) if the auditor agrees. That bridge letter is an attestation from Redwood and not an extension of the independent SOC report itself.
- Separately, we can pull raw system logs for Oct 1-2 (we have a CSV extract for relevant services) and include them with a cover note. Note those logs would be supporting evidence, not covered by the Type II opinion unless the auditor issues a bridge letter.

I'm attaching the SOC2 PDF we issued (redacted for any customer identifiers) and a draft bridge-letter template we usually use. If you want the logs themselves we can produce a short extract (system_logs_oct01-02.csv) for your review.

Next steps I suggest: 
1) Confirm whether your procurement/audit gate needs the bridge letter or just raw logs.
2) If you need the bridge, let me know and I will loop in our auditor (Taylor) and Legal for quick sign-off.

Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123
attachments: SOC2_TypeII_Report_2026-09-30.pdf, Draft_Bridge_Letter_Oct2026.docx

Date: 2026-10-18T11:20:00-04:00
Subject: FW: Question on SOC 2 Type II report dates — quick review request

Laura / Vivek — forwarding a request from Acme. They found two events on Oct 1 and Oct 2 and want to know if those days are covered or if we should issue a bridge letter. I told them the report cuts off at 23:59:59 UTC on Sep 30 and that we can offer a bridge letter through Oct 15 pending auditor agreement.

Can you: 
- Laura: review the attached Draft_Bridge_Letter_Oct2026.docx and flag any legal wording edits (limit scope, no new representations beyond control continuity).
- Vivek: confirm whether Compliance is comfortable with Oct 1-15 as the bridge window and whether we need any extra internal signoffs to provide raw logs for those two days.

I flagged Taylor from the audit firm on the outbound reply — if we get buy-in I can ask Taylor to email a formal bridge attestation.

Quoted original below.

—Ben
attachments forwarded: Draft_Bridge_Letter_Oct2026.docx
From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: ben_carter@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Cc: security@acme.com
Date: 2026-10-18T13:03:00-04:00
Subject: Re: FW: Question on SOC 2 Type II report dates — quick review request

Ben / Vivek / Dawn — reviewed the draft bridge letter. A couple of suggested edits: 
- Add explicit date range (Oct 1—Oct 15, 2026) in the first paragraph and state that the bridge letter "is provided for the limited purpose of vendor evidence to prospective customers and does not expand the scope of the independent SOC 2 Type II report."
- Limit representations to control continuity and do not attempt to restate auditor findings or imply a new audit.
- Add a line noting that raw logs provided are unredacted and subject to our data-sharing policy (we can provide CSV extract but customer must confirm receipt and retention limits).

If Vivek confirms the compliance ok, I can finalize the language and we can ask Taylor to sign.

Laura Bennett
Sr. Counsel, Redwood Inference

Hi all — Taylor here from ThirdPartyAudits. Thanks for looping me in. Confirming current stance: our SOC 2 Type II opinion covers through 2026-09-30 23:59:59 UTC. We can issue a short-form bridge letter dated Oct 19, 2026 that specifically states: 
- Inspector verified there were no material control changes discovered in our follow-up review for the window Oct 1—Oct 15, 2026, subject to Redwood providing supporting evidence (logs, configuration snapshots) within 5 business days.
- Bridge letter will be limited to "no material changes to controls" language and will not constitute a re-issue or expansion of the original report.

If Redwood (Ben / Laura / Vivek) approves the final wording and provides the requested artifacts (we recommend the system_logs_oct01-02.csv and a short config snapshot), I will sign and return the bridge letter.

Taylor Gomez
Principal Auditor, ThirdPartyAudits
